top_choice_rationale: P002 rests on a sharp prediction (Bistritzer and MacDonald, 2011: flat bands at the magic angle) followed by an unexpected experimental discovery (Jarillo-Herrero group, 2018: correlated insulators and superconductivity at that angle), since reproduced by many groups and in other moire materials. The open pairing mechanism does not undermine a citation that honours flat-band-driven correlated phases, and the three names map directly onto the prediction and the discovery. The omission of Yuan Cao is a real cost under the three-name cap, but I rank P001 a close second: it has a clean two-name credit and a distinct magic-wavelength concept, and I would accept it. Both rank above no award.
